'''Alexander Georgiev Petrov ''' ({{langx|bg|Александър Георгиев Петров}}; 27 May 1948 – 22 September 2024) was a Bulgarian professor of [[physics]] and a Fellow of the [[Bulgarian Academy of Sciences]].<ref name = "Marquis Who's Who">{{cite book |chapter= PETROV, Alexander Georgiev |title=Marquis Who's Who in the World |publisher= Reed Elsevier |place= New Providence, NJ |edition= 14th 1997 |year = 1996 |url=https://archive.org/details/whoswhoinworld190000unse/page/n5/mode/2up |url-access= registration |page=[https://archive.org/details/whoswhoinworld190000unse/page/1135/mode/2up 1135] |via= [[Internet Archive]] |accessdate= 22 January 2026}}</ref> 

==Biography==
Petrov was born in [[Stara Zagora]], Bulgaria on 27 May 1948. He had a master's degree in [[atomic physics]] from the [[Sofia University]] (1970) and held a Ph.D. on liquid crystals from the [[Institute of Solid State Physics (Bulgaria)|Institute of Solid State Physics]] (1974). He received a Doctor of Sciences (D.Sc.) degree in 1987, a full Professorship in 1990 and was elected a Fellow of the Bulgarian Academy of Sciences in 2003.

Petrov died on 22 September 2024, at the age of 76.<ref>[https://www.bas.bg/?p=51635 Скръбна вест – акад. Александър Петров] {{in lang|bg}}</ref>

==Area==
The main area of his research was [[soft matter physics]] ([[liquid crystal]]s, [[biophysics]], [[biomolecular]] [[electronics]] and [[nanophysics]]). He worked in the [[Institute of Solid State Physics (Bulgaria)|Institute of Solid State Physics]] at the [[Bulgarian Academy of Sciences]].

==Research==
Petrov investigated theoretically and experimentally dielectric, elastic, flexoelectric and surface properties of nematic liquid crystals with different types of molecular asymmetry. This achievement has applications in liquid-crystal [[optoelectronics]]. In the [[Tissue (biology)|living matter]] [[physics]] he created the knowledge of bioflexoelectricity, including a new theoretical model for description of the [[Elasticity (physics)|elasticity]] and [[flexoelectricity]] of [[biological membrane]]s from the general [[Molecule|molecular]] asymmetry point of view.

He discovered gradient flexoelectric [[Causality|effect]] in nematic liquid crystals under the action of inhomogeneous electric fields (1971–1974); flexoelectric [[oscillation]]s in [[nematic]] [[liquid crystal]]s (1975–1979); direct flexoeffect in biological membrane with [[ion channel]]s (1988–1993); helielectricity in [[chiral]] [[lyotropic]] [[lipid]] [[Phase (matter)|phases]] ([[aqueous]] and nonaqueous) (1988–1989); inverse flexoeffect of bilayer [[lipid membrane]]s (1993); photoflexoeffect in photo-active membranes (1992–1994).<ref>Jubilee Collection. 30th Anniversary of the Institute of Solid State Physics Bulgarian Academy of Sciences 1972 — 2002, Sofia, 2002 ({{ISBN|954-91198-1-5}})</ref>

==Professional experience==
*Director of the [[Institute of Solid State Physics (Bulgaria)|Institute of Solid State Physics]] at the [[Bulgarian Academy of Sciences]] (since 1999 up to 2015)
*Head of Biomolecular Layers Laboratory, ISSP-BAS (1991–2008)
*Petrov was a Head of Soft Matter Physics Division of ISSP-BAS (since 2006 up to 2016).

==Awards==
Petrov was awarded the Freedericksz Medal for outstanding contributions in the field of liquid crystal physics by the Russian Liquid Crystal Society (2004), the Outstanding Contribution to Science Annual Award of the Ministry of Education and Science of Bulgaria (Scientist of the year 2007) and the Marin Drinov Sign of Honour of Bulgarian Academy of Sciences on a ribbon (2008).
